chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:

Zurārah asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about salat (prayer) in garments made from foxes, fennec, squirrel, and other fur. So he brought out a book which he claimed was the dictation of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.

"Indeed, salat (prayer) in the fur of every thing whose eating is forbidden is invalid; thus salat (prayer) in its fur, hair, skin, urine, dung, and every thing from it is invalid. That salat (prayer) is not accepted until he prays in something other than it, from what Allah has made lawful to eat."

Then he said: "O Zurārah, this is from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and by Allah, preserve this, O Zurārah. For if it is from that whose flesh is eaten, then salat (prayer) in its fur, urine, hair, dung, milk, and every thing from it is permissible, if you know that it is properly slaughtered and that slaughter has purified it. But if it is other than that, from what you have been forbidden to eat or what has been made unlawful for you to eat, then salat (prayer) in every thing from it is invalid, whether slaughter has purified it or not."
And (819) 27 - Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Hamadhānī, who said:
I wrote to him: fur and hair from what is not eaten falls upon my garment, without taqiyyah or necessity. So he wrote: "Salat (prayer) in it is not permissible."

key_terms.الذَّبْحُ: slaughter; the act by which an animal is rendered lawfully purified where applicable
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.الْوَبَرِ: fur, especially animal fur used in clothing or found on garments
key_terms.تَقِيَّةٍ: dissimulation under constraint; mentioned here as an exception context
key_terms.جَائِزَةٌ: permissible or valid in the legal sense
key_terms.حَرَامٍ: forbidden; describing animals whose flesh is unlawful to eat
key_terms.ذَكِيٌّ: properly slaughtered according to the prescribed legal method
key_terms.فَاسِدَةٌ: invalid; legally unsound and not accepted

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) valid in clothing made from the fur or hair of animals whose meat is forbidden to eat?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the legal ruling that salat (prayer) is invalid in anything derived from animals whose flesh is forbidden to eat, including their fur, hair, skin, urine, and dung. It also states that what comes from animals whose flesh is lawful to eat may be used in salat (prayer), provided the animal was properly slaughtered where required. The report emphasizes the authority of the ruling by attributing it to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.
